scope: Read-only source review plus isolated independent Windows probes; no models, SSH, external network, deployment or product edits.

method_recall.application: Pinned actual source and tested cancellation/physical settlement separately from content approval. Same-host transport success does not prove cross-machine or live-model acceptance.

checks.meaning: Three successful reproductions of defects, not passing product acceptance.
Existing real HTTP/separate-process comprehensive scenario independently rerun on exact source.

blockers.title: A revoked offer poisons the node event batch and prevents later cancellation
blockers.reproduction: Reserve a and b on one capacity-2 node; enqueue cancel(b); revoke producer read/receive for a; events(token,0,timeout=0) raises NativeStoreError on both attempts while cancel(b) remains in durable ledger.
blockers.impact: No response means node cannot advance its cursor; HTTP 409 terminates serve, or current workflow permission failure causes 500 and endless unchanged retries. Unrelated valid work and cancellation cannot progress.
blockers.fix_acceptance: Deliver a cursor-advancing minimal withdrawal/no-launch event for invalidated offers without exposing task content; later valid offers and cancels must remain consumable under continued revocation.

blockers.title: Recovery executes a producer synchronously outside cancellation tracking
blockers.reproduction: Persist received row and advanced cursor before intent (valid crash window). Run recover(); actual NativeWorker producer starts, active has no execution. Enqueue server cancellation while real process runs; recover blocks until natural process completion, cursor remains unchanged, output cancelled=false.
blockers.impact: serve invokes recover before step; recovery workers cannot receive cancellation for their entire run (potentially installed timeout). Capacity also recovers sequentially. This is the ordinary continuous service path, not the documented --once limitation.
blockers.fix_acceptance: Recovered received-without-intent work must use the same bounded executor/active cancellation path as new offers while event consumption continues. Prove real parent/descendant cancellation during recovery; existing unknown intent must still never relaunch.

blockers.title: Physical settlement depends on the revoked original user and leaks global capacity
blockers.reproduction: Reserve execution then revoke w.authorize for its original actor. Trusted matching physical closure writes remote closed=1; receipt calls workflow.reconcile(original actor), whose initial status raises PermissionDenied. native_tasks stays running.
blockers.impact: Node slot is closed but global capacity counts running/held/reserved forever. HTTP failure/replay cannot repair while revocation persists. Existing producer-intake revocation test does not cover user coordination ACL withdrawal.
blockers.fix_acceptance: Use a narrowly authorized physical-settlement path that closes global ownership without granting original actor content/read privileges. Revoke current user ACL, submit trusted exact physical closure, verify global and node capacity release, candidate absent, and replay stable.

source_review_positive: Narrow node mount authenticates separately from ProductionAccess; baseline confirms node credential rejected by ordinary models API.
Assignments bind tenant/node/profile/installation/package/task; node verifies exact task and local installation before prepare.
Node cache and approval records are not imported as server candidates; server reconstructs its own current-authority intake.
Durable intent prevents restart relaunch; baseline verifies coordinator OS lock, actual descendant closure and physical/output mismatch rejection.
Explicit installed factory and rollback instructions exist, but actual cross-machine installation/rollback is not demonstrated by this review.
remaining_unproven: Cross-machine server/node operation and actual installation/rollback
Real model efficiency/quality and parent AA
